candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — related activity statements: advocate for client rights and needs; collaborate with members of the interprofessional team; perform procedures necessary to safely transfer/discharge clients and follow up unresolved client-care issues
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Advocacy/Continuity of Care / access barriers and resource coordination
candidate.educational_objective: Identify social and structural barriers to care and advocate for coordinated resources that improve a client's ability to access follow-up care and prescribed treatment.

options.A: Assess the transportation and financial barriers and collaborate with the appropriate care-management or community resources to improve access
options.B: Document the client as noncompliant because attendance is the client's responsibility
options.C: Tell the client to stop prescribed medications until transportation becomes affordable
options.D: Provide the same appointment instructions again without addressing the stated access barriers

candidate.rationale: Healthy People 2030 identifies transportation, income, health-care access, and medication affordability as social determinants that can limit access to needed care and contribute to health disparities. NCSBN's 2026 Management of Care activity statements require the RN to advocate for client rights and needs and coordinate care. Assessing the stated barriers and connecting the client with appropriate resources addresses the underlying access problem; labeling the client, stopping therapy, or repeating instructions without addressing the barriers does not. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Financial and transportation barriers can limit access to care and medications and contribute to health disparities; addressing access barriers is relevant to improving health equity.
candidate.source_document_title: Healthy People 2030 — Social Determinants of Health; Access to Health Services
candidate.source_locator: Social Determinants of Health: SDOH include transportation, income, health-care access, language/literacy and other environmental conditions that affect health outcomes; Access to Health Services literature summary: barriers include lack of insurance, out-of-pocket costs, transportation problems and limited health-care resources, and these barriers can contribute to poor outcomes and disparities
candidate.source_organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services — Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion
candidate.stem: A client repeatedly misses follow-up appointments and says, 'I cannot afford the bus fare and sometimes have to choose between transportation and paying for my medicines.' Which nursing action best addresses the health-equity barrier?
